column2: INTRODUCTION

This equipment is necessary to allow the Service Police Crime Bureau (SPCB) to conduct their investigations to their optimal capability.

column2: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply and delivery to the Nuclear Department at HMS Sultan, of experimental apparatus which is to be used to examine the performance characteristics of a number of candidate test materials in the presence of flowing high temperature and pressure aqueous fluids. To include a minimum 1 year warranty, costings for subsequent annual safety assessments, ½ day familiarisation training (to be delivered within 3 weeks of receipt), taking test equipment up to full pressure and temperature conditions and an operating manual. The output should include a front control panel with adjacent test oven. Delivery should be against the technical specification as defined in the Statement of Requirement (SOR)

The requirement is for a HP/HT fluid flow rig made of stainless steel construction to enable the pumping of test aqueous fluid through a specific test column. The test column will be located in a suitable oven environment and housed vertically with inlet fluid at the top, exiting at the bottom. Furthermore the test column must be of suitable dimensions to allow the containment of test organic or mineral material and be fitted with a bottom mesh to support the test solids, whilst still allowing fluid flow through the column. It will be important for the test column to be readily removed from the test rig and be amenable to easy discharge and subsequent re-filling with test material prior to use again. Test conditions up to 200 bar and 300°C are required.
The MoD will require a “rough” Computer Aided Design (CAD) drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to display full rig assembly and functionality.
The delivery and installation is to be no later than 31 Mar 2016.

JFC9/00002 - ITT Docs,Contract,"MINISTRY OF DEFENCE",Awarded,2016-02-15T11:09:54Z,"TRANSPARENCY ONLY-DOCUMENTS PROVIDED FOR TRANSPARENCY ONLY IN RELATION TO: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)","NOTE: This notice was updated on 10 February 2016 for the following reason: Change to EOI deadline to fit with business needs.1. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department. 2. The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety. As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3. 3. The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered. 4. It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system. The new system should allow for a short, timed, interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data). In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area. Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students). 5. The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality. 6. BIP41072649,Contract,"Ministry of Defence, Agencies/Misc, Other",Awarded,2016-04-25T16:03:03+01:00,"GB-Bristol: Land Vehicle Exercise (LVEX) SBRI Phase 2-Signature Reduction MOLLE","LVEx will contribute towards efforts to return to Contingent Operations by identification, prioritisation and evaluation of equipments and concepts designed to improve the Mounted Close Combat (MCC) capability.
This competition is divided into two separate strands.

column2: COTS - Mature “Commercial off the Shelf” (COTS) equipment, which is ready to be tested in a military context will be considered.

SBRI - Novel concepts and applications, including COTS offerings currently applied in non-defence areas that require R&D to make them applicable to defence needs are sought in order to provide innovative solutions.

column1: Ultimately this will help MoD to de-risk procurement, generate evidence of capability gaps and inform requirements for future Equipment Programmes.
LVEx 2013 focuses on four key themes. Industry is invited to submit COTS technologies with innovative applications, or concepts that could provide solutions to any or all of the themes:

column2: Mobility - We are looking for innovative ways to enhance the mobility of our vehicles over difficult terrain. Platforms of interest are those of our vehicles weighing 40 tonnes and below.
Signature Reduction - We are interested in solutions for reducing the visual, acoustic and electronic signatures of our vehicle fleet i.e. how easy it is for our vehicles to be seen, heard or sensed.

Weight saving - We are very interested to see solutions which demonstrate how technology could reduce the weight of our wheeled vehicles. Platform types of interest include all those vehicles weighing 20 tonnes and below e.g. Ridgeback, Jackal, Coyote, Husky, etc.

Stowage - We invite industry to demonstrate innovative solutions for optimising internal and external stowage across our entire vehicle fleet. Specific problems include: stowage of personal kit, stowage of individual weapons due to the lack of a universal weapon rack, external Stowage of fuel, Electronic Counter Measures and water (all of which will also require protection).

column1: Technologies developed and equipment shall be evaluated and the performance and effectiveness demonstrated through the established MOD Level A-B-C trials process:

column2: Level A – System Performance evaluation (paper assessment/system demonstration)
Level B – Fight-ability (soldier field tests)/System performance capture
Level C – User Performance & System Effectiveness (vignette trials)

DTEC/225,Contract,"MINISTRY OF DEFENCE",Awarded,2016-04-26T07:03:57+01:00,"Land Vehicle Exercise (LVEX) SBRI Phase2 - ISTEC Signature Reduction Molle","PHASE 2 ACTIVITY

Phase 1 activity ISTEC developed the camouflage concept into a demonstrator suitable for fitment to a Protected Weapon Station. For Phase 2 it is expected that a prototype solution covering a complete platform will be supplied.

The whole platform solution will then be tested and demonstrated against current in-service camouflage to quantify the benefits of the system with respect to Visual, Near Infra-Red (Image intensifier) and Far Infra-Red (Thermal) signature. Radar signature is not to be considered.

The MOLLE stowage concepts shall be carried forward through further development, considering weight distribution, ergonomics and accessibility. These will exist only on inner surfaces of the platform, and where is deemed useful by the designer, after consideration of common uses and configurations.

Ease of application, replacement and maintenance shall also be considered with a focus on the simplicity of the aforementioned by non-technical users wherever possible. Trials are likely to examine some aspects of this. Environmental robustness must be considered throughout. Due to the lack of environmental sealing, some consideration must be given to the effect of water saturation on the solutions weight, usability and fitting.

Whilst creating a whole platform solution it will be required to consider as a design exercise and feasibility study, the fitment of the solution to another/modified platform (TBD at kick-off), which is likely to be fitted with armour packs for theatre and/or may have a number of additional retrofitted equipment.

BIP41203628,Contract,"Ministry of Defence, C&C, Other",Awarded,2016-04-28T08:36:02+01:00,"GB-swindon: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)","1.
column2: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department.

The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety.   As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3.
The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered.

It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system.  The new system should allow for a short, timed,  interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data).  In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area.  Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students).
The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality.

The Authority envisages a need for a brief site survey to enable potential suppliers to inspect the facility and compile accurate measurements of the installation site. This is planned to take place on 15 Feb 16 13:30.
The Authority has the desire for delivery and installation by the end of Mar 2016

BIP47463557,Contract,"Ministry of Defence, C&C, Other",Awarded,2016-09-29T11:03:00+01:00,"GB-swindon: The design, supply, delivery, and installation of laser safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA)","1.
column2: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has a requirement for the design, supply, delivery, and installation of safety equipment necessary to create a Laser Controlled Area (LCA) within one of the laboratory spaces used by the Nuclear Department.

The Nuclear Department owns a Class 4 Laser which can be used to image water flowing in an acrylic channel. The laser will be operated in the ND Irradiation Facility in a room which is shared with other scientific equipment. To allow simultaneous use of the facility, which is a requirement, a Laser Controlled Area must be established in accordance with JSP 390 – Military Laser Safety.   As this system will be operated in a laboratory environment, the most relevant section is JSP 390 Volume 1 Issue 3 Section 3.
The expected engineered solution is described in paragraph 4 however, other solutions that satisfy the requirements will also be considered.

It is expected that the most cost effective way to establish the LCA is to divide the room into two areas using a laser blocking material which must comply with IEC 60825-4:2006 in the pitched roof space and a curtain, complying to the same specification, hanging below the trusses. The curtain is to be attached at each end to walls by an interlocked connection. Above the curtain, a laser blocking material must be used to fill the spaces between trusses which support the roof. A new interlock system is also required to replace the existing obsolete system.  The new system should allow for a short, timed,  interlock override to allow safe ingress/egress from the area while the laser is functioning (often the laser will need to run continuously for hours at a time to generate data).  In addition, the new interlock should be connected to external signs which indicate the state of the laser to anyone outside the laser controlled area.  Personal Protective Equipment (Eyewear) is also required for 5 people (based on the instructor plus 4 students).
The MoD will require a full description and “rough” drawing to be submitted at the tender stage to identify the proposed solution and safety functionality.

The Authority envisages a need for a brief site survey to enable potential suppliers to inspect the facility and compile accurate measurements of the installation site. This is planned to take place on 15 Feb 16 13:30.
The Authority has the desire for delivery and installation by the end of Mar 2016
